statement: manifest.json identifies namespace ownership, protocol version, repository identity, and the supported schema dialect.
dossier.json is the sole canonical truth for current governed state, and only immutable records referenced by that snapshot affect current state.
Handoff, submission, and decision envelopes are immutable create-once records; an unreferenced envelope is reported as an orphan and never applied as current truth.
The locks directory is transient coordination state and is never dossier truth or history.
M0 has no authoritative brief.md; every human-readable view is generated from canonical data so Markdown cannot become a second editable truth.
Repository, dossier, run, handoff, submission, decision, criterion, evidence, operation, and actor identifiers are opaque strings generated or validated by the reference CLI.

Repository, dossier, run, handoff, submission, decision, criterion, and evidence identifiers are never reused within their scope; operation identifiers are unique within one dossier and basis revision.
Human-readable titles are display metadata and never identity.
Revisions are non-negative decimal strings with no leading zero except the value 0.
Digests use the exact sha256:<lowercase-hex> wire grammar.
Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 strings ending in Z, wall-clock time does not order concurrent mutations, and machine fields and codes remain English ASCII and locale invariant.
Governed JSON rejects bytes that are not valid UTF-8 before schema validation.
Governed JSON rejects duplicate object member names after JSON escape decoding before schema validation.
Governed JSON rejects isolated Unicode surrogates and Unicode noncharacters before schema validation.
Protocol JSON rejects numeric values and represents counters and revisions with restricted decimal strings.
Governed JSON rejects a byte-order mark unless that artifact contract explicitly permits it.
Every schema uses JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, and every root declares that dialect and a stable $id.
Protocol version and schema dialect are separate required fields.
Runtime validation resolves only bundled and pinned named root schemas and references, with no network resolution.
Security- and state-critical objects are closed; unknown critical fields and unknown major versions fail closed.
JSON Schema format, default, and examples annotations are never the sole validity or authorization mechanism.
Canonical bytes are UTF-8 RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes of an explicitly named projection and are hashed as lowercase SHA-256 wire digests.
Canonicalization preserves array order and does not normalize Unicode, so NFC and NFD strings remain distinct.
State revision, state digest, content digest, observed-evidence digest, checks digest, and submission digest remain six distinct protocol concepts.
The dossier-state projection contains every canonical dossier field except state_digest and invents no other exclusion.
The content projection contains exactly dossier ID, objective, scope, constraints, ordered criteria, and ordered evidence with every declared field except captured_at.
The observed-evidence projection contains the exact specified fields, preserves dossier evidence order, sorts limitation codes in ASCII order, and excludes unstable filesystem and diagnostic data.
External references and human observations project human_review_required with null observed artifact digest and size.
The checks projection contains the exact specified fields, uses protocol-stage then ASCII invariant ordering and criterion order, and excludes state and diagnostic metadata.
Checks fail for any failed invariant, unsatisfied mechanical criterion, or unlinked recorded-human criterion; human_review_required alone is not failure or substantive approval.

Assignment, locks, display timestamps, orphan records, and filesystem observations do not change content_digest; adding registered evidence does, and changed artifact bytes stale dependent envelopes without silently changing stored revision or content digest.
The manifest contains exactly the specified protocol, protocol version, schema dialect, repository ID, and creation timestamp fields.
The dossier snapshot contains the complete specified brief, revision, self-digest, last-operation, active-run, evidence, and current-envelope-pointer fields.
Evidence records use a closed kind-tagged shape and require artifact digest and size for local file and captured command-result artifacts.

Local evidence paths are slash-separated repository-relative lexical paths and fail closed on absolute, drive, UNC, backslash, empty, dot, dot-dot, NUL, linked, reparse, escaping, or aliased resolution.
M0 mechanically validates local file and captured command-result evidence; external references and human observations remain human-review data and cannot satisfy mechanical criteria.

All criteria are conjunctive; one current linked local artifact mechanically satisfies a mechanical criterion, linked artifacts are alternatives, and a recorded-human criterion requires linked evidence but remains human_review_required.

A submission has the exact specified digest-bound fields, excludes only submission_digest from its self-projection, is legal only for the active run with passing checks and no unaccepted handoff, then advances the snapshot pointer and clears the decision pointer.
Checks, review, acceptance, and handoff states are derived and are never stored as a free-standing DONE field or mutable checks cache.
check, show, and submission creation recompute current checks from canonical state and present evidence observations.

ready_for_review requires a referenced submission whose covered content, observations, and checks still match; accepted additionally requires a referenced acceptance decision for the still-current submission digest.
Covered-content change stales dependent submissions, unaccepted handoffs, and decisions; rejection yields changes_requested and a later submission is a new immutable envelope.
M0 provides no dossier abandonment, archival, reopening, deletion, or purge transition, and material brief changes require a new dossier.
Every governed mutation creates the dossier writer guard with an exclusive-create primitive before reading current state.

After guard acquisition, every governed mutation validates the current snapshot, compares exact revision, state digest, and operation identity, and validates one complete next snapshot before publication.
Snapshot publication stages a temporary file in the target directory, flushes and closes it under the profile, and publishes with one profile replacement primitive.
A governed mutation reopens and validates the published snapshot and releases the writer guard only after verification.

Idempotency is scoped to dossier, basis revision, and operation ID: an identical immediate retry returns the prior success, an older replay conflicts, and same-basis operation reuse with different input fails.
A writer lock records guard ID, exact basis, creation time, and declared-profile process identity; age makes it only possibly stale and never authorizes automatic takeover.

Guard recovery first obtains a separate exclusive recovery guard, visibly excludes writers and other recovery, requires interactive confirmation and proven process termination, quarantines the old guard, revalidates state, publishes a guarded no-op revision, verifies it, and only then releases recovery exclusivity.

Recovery stops with recovery-required when prior-writer termination is live, unavailable, or inconclusive; the one-writer guarantee resumes only after proven termination and completed profile-specific recovery.

Handoff, submission, and decision publication validates preconditions under the guard, creates and validates the immutable envelope, replaces the snapshot pointer, verifies referenced state, and then releases the guard.
A crash before pointer publication may leave an orphan envelope, but the orphan has no authority over current state.
Envelope IDs derive from operation IDs; the first create fixes persisted IDs and timestamps, an identical retry reuses and validates them, and a conflicting same-ID envelope fails closed.
A handoff envelope contains the exact specified offer fields and stores no status or status-basis member; offer state is derived.
Only the active run can create a handoff offer, and creating it records but does not transfer responsibility.
The offer binds the validated pre-offer revision and digest, deterministic next published revision, and offered content digest without self-referential snapshot digest.
Acceptance must match intended actor, exact published revision, offered content digest, active run, current handoff pointer, and independently validated current state-digest precondition.
Successful acceptance creates the recipient run and atomically updates active actor, run ID, and started-by-handoff pointer; the previous run immediately loses write authority.
Before acceptance, a later governed mutation that changes a required acceptance precondition makes the offer stale; there is no cancellation operation or cancellation history.
Actor labels are recorded claims and never authenticated identities.
Accepted handoff is derived only from matching current handoff, started-by-handoff, recipient actor, and valid immutable offer, and successful acceptance is terminal for that envelope.
Ordinary work after acceptance does not retroactively stale the accepted handoff, while a later handoff replaces the current reference.

check is read-only, never advances state revision, and reports parsing, schema/version, cross-file, evidence-safety, evidence-integrity, envelope-integrity, digest, and derived-status stages distinctly.
Submission creation reruns checks after acquiring the writer guard, stores no mutable checks result, and embeds current content, observation, and checks digests.
Later show and check recompute observations and compare them to the referenced submission to derive currentness.
A validator exception is an internal error and can never produce a valid result.

Local artifact validation uses open-read-validate-close and rejects outside-root, linked, reparse, directory, disallowed-empty, missing, and byte-mismatched evidence without overstating what passing checks prove.
An acceptance or rejection envelope contains the exact specified fields and binds one exact submission digest with recorded-interactive-claim identity assurance.
criteria_reviewed exactly equals the submitted dossier's complete criterion-ID list in canonical criterion order; partial acceptance is unavailable.
A decision is legal only for the snapshot's exact current submission ID and digest; older or non-current submissions fail even when covered digests happen to match.

Every decision, including orphan recovery, requires an interactive display of exact submission and criteria plus the explicit phrase; no --yes or non-interactive path exists, and output calls it Recorded Human Acceptance rather than authenticated approval.
The reference CLI exposes only the eleven specified M0 commands plus its version request.
Dossier creation creates the initial active run for the recorded actor with a null started-by-handoff pointer.
Every dossier-scoped command requires an explicit dossier ID and M0 never guesses a current, recent, or sole dossier.
Every mutation requires an operation ID, and every existing-dossier mutation requires exact expected revision and state digest in machine mode.
Human mode may omit a basis only after the same invocation displays and confirms the complete basis and transition; the later guarded comparison never silently rebinds to intervening state.

After --json is detected, every normal result is exactly one result envelope on stdout, stderr has no machine-required information, warnings remain structured, and consumers branch only on stable code and process exit independent of locale.
Every stable symbolic result code maps to its specified process-exit class, and exact callers inspect the symbolic code.
No error recommends destructive deletion as its default remediation.
dossier show presents the bounded specified current material, reports unresolved proof limitations, and recommends exactly one next valid action.
JSON mode exposes the complete structured view while default human output remains bounded and points to deeper data instead of embedding large evidence.
Repository-root discovery starts at the current directory, resolves the owning version-control worktree when available, and displays the resolved root before mutation.
Initialization creates only .case-agent and changes no byte outside that namespace.
Existing incompatible, partial, linked, junctioned, or unknown .case-agent content fails closed as a collision before writes.
Repeating the same compatible initialization is byte-idempotent.
An unsupported newer major namespace remains read-only inspectable and is never modified.
M0 initialization never modifies .gitignore, host instructions, hooks, PATH, or user-global configuration.
Nested repositories, submodules, linked worktrees, case aliases, UNC, cloud-sync, and clone-with-active-writer targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Core commands perform zero network access.
Schemas, runtime conformance data, and human help are bundled for offline use.
M0 performs no update checks and emits no telemetry.
The tool does not claim to detect or protect all secrets in dossier content.
Evidence stores references and digests by default and never copies artifact bytes without a later explicit feature.
Uninstalling the CLI never removes .case-agent data, and purge or retention automation is outside M0.
Offline operation never implies supply-chain verification, sandboxing, privacy certification, or protection from other local processes.

A claimed POSIX local profile creates target-directory temporaries and create-once files exclusively, uses the declared local rename primitive, fully reads and validates snapshots, proves termination before recovery, and distinguishes process-crash safety from power-loss durability.

A claimed Windows local profile creates same-volume target-directory temporaries and CREATE_NEW-equivalent files, uses one supported replacement primitive, permits required delete sharing for readers, proves process identity before recovery, bounds visible sharing retries, and verifies target state after replace failure.
The public support matrix lists only real platform profiles that pass the complete frozen corpus.
The host-neutral protocol claims only filesystem behavior proven by the active declared profile; a controlled-test adapter is test capability and never production-platform support.
Every normative executable requirement has every declared positive and negative direction covered by an actually executed discriminating vector.
Every conformance case is a schema-validated closed fixture_version 1 object containing every specified case, tree, invocation, expectation, and derived-view field explicitly.
Every content, stdin, stdout, and view reference resolves to a regular file inside the frozen corpus, and every declared input digest matches before execution.

Initial and expected tree paths are safe, unique, ordered repository-relative paths, and fresh repositories are populated without traversal, absolute, drive, UNC, backslash, link, reparse, alias, or duplicate-path escape.
Random IDs, clocks, retry timing, locale, process identity, environment, platform behavior, and network denial are fixed by deterministic case adapters.

Sequential and grouped concurrent invocations execute the same dispatcher and workflows; invocation and expectation counts match, concurrent allowed results are explicit, and exactly-one-success constraints are enforced.

The frozen corpus executes every blocking initialization, JSON/schema/JCS, writer, retry, publication-fault, guard, evidence, handoff, submission, decision, version/internal, rehydration, platform-text/path, and offline family.
Explicit validator or fault mutation proves that state-critical corruption turns a formerly passing vector red, and expectation changes cannot be trusted as success.
Before adding a skill or second-host adapter, the baseline comparison covers competing writers, stale handoff acceptance, changed accepted artifacts, and evidence that no longer matches.

The baseline compares ordinary Markdown plus Git against the L0 reference CLI without a skill, using correct detection without false success as the primary metric and the specified burden measures as secondary metrics.
M0 advances only after detecting all four target failures with documented acceptable burden, and that result never justifies broader reliability claims.
M0 is not releasable until the normative L0 specification and schema projections are complete.
M0 is not releasable until every executable MUST has its required positive and negative fixtures.
M0 is not releasable until the full frozen corpus passes on every claimed real platform profile.
M0 is not releasable unless race tests produce exactly one successful conforming mutation.
M0 is not releasable if direct-edit, stale-evidence, stale-handoff, or stale-acceptance fixtures can become green, or if validator exceptions do not fail closed.
M0 is not releasable until the complete walking skeleton succeeds without network access and a context-loss run resumes from the bounded current view.
M0 is not releasable until the Markdown baseline comparison is recorded.

Release documentation makes no unsupported identity, audit, sandbox, enterprise, weak-model, or reliability claim, an independent review finds no spec/schema/CLI/fixture contradiction, and preview claims remain limited to demonstrated file-native, invariant, handoff, and exact platform-profile results.
